newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-RODMAN GETS OVATION, JORDAN GETS 43 POINTS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-RODMAN GETS OVATION, JORDAN GETS 43 POINTS.

text.p: Michael Jordan scored 43 points, including a 25-footer at the buzzer that gave the Chicago Bulls a 103-100 victory over the Charlotte Hornets on Tuesday.
Dennis Rodman returned from an 11-game suspension for kicking a cameraman and grabbed 14 rebounds. Rodman received a rousing ovation from the sellout crowd at the United Centre.
"I though I played like (bleep) tonight," Rodman said. "My timing was off, but we won, so that's all that matters. It was great to be back in front of the fans."
Among the crowd was Rodman's father, Philander, to whom Rodman has not spoken in 30 years.
"I don't know if I'm going to see my father," Rodman said. "The only reason he's here is because I'm the only one in the family who has any money."
Rodman received the second-longest suspension in NBA history for kicking cameraman Eugene Amos in a game January 15th.
In Cleveland, Chris Mills had 22 points and 10 rebounds as the Cleveland Cavaliers had six players in double figures to defeat the Philadelphia 76ers, 105-94, for the ninth consecutive time.
Tyrone Hill also had a season-high 22 points and 10 rebounds and Bobby Sura added 14 for Cleveland, which had lost four of its last five games.
In Dallas, Vernon Maxwell scored a season-high 34 points and Vinny Del Negro added 18 as the San Antonio Spurs stopped a six-game losing streak with a 111-97 victory over the Dallas Mavericks.
Maxwell shot 7-for-11 from three-point range and almost outscored the Mavericks' starters, who had just 38 points. Carl Herrera scored 14 points and Avery Johnson 13 assists and nine points.

In Houston, Kevin Willis and Brent Price each scored 20 points off the bench as the Houston Rockets used a key 16-0 run for a 106-97 victory over the Vancouver Grizzlies, snapping a six-game losing streak.
Rockets All-Star forward Charles Barkley had 13 points and eight assists as he returned from a sprained right ankle.

In Los Angeles, Malik Sealy scored 21 points and Loy Vaught added 18, including a key jumper with 82 seconds left, as the Los Angeles Clippers won their fourth consecutive game, 116-112 over the Boston Celtics.
Rodney Rogers also scored 18 points and Eric Piatkowski added 15 for los Angeles.
In Miami, Tim Hardaway scored 17 of his 31 points in the third quarter as the Miami Heat won their seventh consecutive game with a 104-91 victory over the Detroit Pistons.
Hardaway added 10 assists and three steals. Alonzo Mourning had 29 points, 11 rebounds and five blocks for the Heat.
Grant Hill scored 17 points and Terry Mills added 15 for Detroit.

In Milwaukee, Vin Baker had eight points and a pair of key blocked shots in the final four minutes as the Milwaukee Bucks snapped a five-game losing streak with a 101-96 victory over the Toronto Raptors.
Baker finished with 23 points and nine rebounds and Ray Allen added 19 points for the Bucks, who had dropped 15 of their last 21 games.
In Orlando, Khalid Reeves made a pair of three-pointers down the stretch as the New Jersey Nets snapped a seven-game losing streak to the Orlando Magic with a 104-98 victory.
Kendall Gill had 28 points and eight assists, and Kerry Kittles had 25 and Reeves finished with 19 points for New Jersey.
In Portland, Kenny Anderson scored 19 of his 33 points in the fourth quarter as the Portland Trail Blazers snapped a five-game losing streak with a 111-108 victory over the Phoenix Suns.

Anderson made five foul shots in the final 21 seconds, including one with 10.9 seconds left that gave Portland a three-point lead. Phoenix guards Wesley Person and Kevin Johnson missed three-pointers in the waning seconds.

In Sacramento, Karl Malone scored all 30 of his points in the first three quarters as the Utah Jazz exploded for a season high in points, continuing their mastery of the Sacramento Kings with a 120-98 victory.
Shandon Anderson scored 20 to lead the Jazz.
In Seattle, Gary Payton scored 28 points and Sam Perkins had all 11 of his during a key second-quarter run as the Seattle SuperSonics snapped a two-game skid with a 108-81 rout of the Denver Nuggets.
Payton added nine assists. Shawn Kemp scored 12 points, and Hersey Hawkins and Jim McIlvaine each added 11 for Seattle.

In Washington, Patrick Ewing and John Starks scored 18 points apiece as the New York Knicks spoiled the debut of Washington coach Bernie Bickerstaff and continued their domination of the Bullets 97-92.
Allan Houston added 17 points for the Knicks, who defeated the Bullets for the fifth straight time and 20th in the last 21 meetings.
